note: Free open primitive camping along the dirt roads around the Blair Valley dry lakebed, off S-2 in Anza-Borrego. The park's road report (October 2026) rates the first half mile of camps fine for two-wheel drive; beyond that the road is sandy. Pack out trash. --Claude
summary: Blair Valley (Anza-Borrego): confirmed free, first-come, 30-day calendar-year limit, vault toilets, no water; current park road report says the first half mile of camps is 2WD-OK, then sandy (flagged, keep); pin at the S-2 turnoff is fine.
flags: ACCESS (keep, caveat in note): park road conditions updated 10/30/2026 read 'Blair Valley ... First ½ mile of camps ok for 2WD, then sandy.' 2WD access to the near camps is stated, so this is not a 4WD drop. The park page's 'Most dirt roads require vehicles with AWD or 4x4' is park-wide boilerplate. The 2017 brochure: 'roads in Blair Valley are usually accessible by two-wheel drive vehicles.'

NOTE: the stored 'accommodates cars to big rigs' (a thedyrt/campsitephotos claim) and 'passable to a normal vehicle in dry conditions' are replaced by the agency's dated road report. The 30-day limit, no water and vault toilets come out because the fields show them.

PIN 33.03731,-116.41044 is at the Blair Valley turnoff, ~105 m W of the first pullouts/vault toilet (~33.0371,-116.4093). Under 250 m, fine. PHONE 760-767-4205 (Visitor Center) matches. WEBSITE is the park page, fine.

LEADS (not in DB, Anza-Borrego primitive camps): Mountain Palm Springs Campground (fee schedule 'Tent/RV Site: $20 per night'; road report 'Sandy', near Bow Willow 11614); Culp Valley Campground (road report 'Upper road is rutted, lower OK'); Yaqui Well ('Soft sand to Yaqui Well'); Arroyo Salado ('Soft sand starting at primitive camp ... high clearance needed', likely out). Fish Creek is listed as 'Tent' only, and Sheep Canyon sits beyond the Coyote Canyon closure.
